rounds.report:
L1 / Proxy reconstruction - CineRecon Three.js sampled-frame baseline (video33, 1280x720, 60 fps, 1122 frames, 18.7 s)

Content (inferred from the 24 timestamped reference samples): one continuous high-angle follow-camera shot, no cuts. A white goose carries a two-roll toilet-paper pack in its beak leftward along a grey street that ends at a dark tiled roof ridge (the roof and brick chimneys sit in the foreground and partly hide the goose around 6.0-7.5 s). A woman (purple sleeves, maroon vest, brown trousers) walks right along the far side of the street from about 7 s, notices the goose at about 10.5 s (thought bubble showing the pack), turns and rushes toward it, bends at about 13 s to pick up the pack the goose dropped, then walks right toward the market stall carrying it while the goose honks and flaps its wings and follows. Background: market stall (red-clothed table with blue trays, toilet-roll stack, A-board, black crates, plant cart), grass patch with curb, bench, lamp pole, green post, puddle, brick building, and a girl kicking a football.

Geometry: boxes, spheres, cylinders, cones and flat polygons only. The goose has a body, neck, head and beak, two legs and two wings as separate parts. The woman has a pelvis, two-segment legs, a bendable torso, a head with hair, and two-segment arms. The pack is two cylinders with a band. Chimneys are brick boxes with a cap and pots. The roof is a set of sloped slabs along a ridge polyline, and the street polygon is clipped at the ridge.

Articulation: goose leg swing and body waddle are tied to the distance walked; the neck tilts (carrying vs. upright), the head lifts during honks, and the wings spread and flap at about 13.5-14.2, 15.1-15.8 and 16.7-18.1 s. Woman: walking/running gait from the distance walked, a torso bend and knee crouch for the pick-up (12.7-13.65 s), and the left arm holding the pack afterwards. Girl: one kick at about 8.9 s, and the ball rolls after it.

Camera and timing: I fitted a perspective camera (vertical FOV 9.9 deg, pitch about 25-28 deg, yaw rotating from about 8 to 32 deg and back to 20 deg, distance zooming from 14 to 20 to 12 units) to static landmarks I marked by hand in all 24 samples (my own least-squares fit). It is interpolated with monotone cubic curves at the sample timestamps. Subject positions come from back-projecting the subjects' ground-contact pixels through the fitted cameras. Every state is computed from absolute time.

Observed vs. inferred: the positions, poses and camera at the 24 sample times are estimated from the reference images. Motion between samples is inferred: walking cadence, the exact timing of the pack drop (about 12.5 s) and pick-up (about 13.3 s), the start of the wing flaps, and the woman's path before she enters the frame.

Feedback: none received yet (initial submission). No render has been inspected.
